title: Statement Regarding the Publication of Reference Rates on Friday, April 3, 2026

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The New York Fed issued an operating policy statement announcing that TGCR, BGCR, SOFR, and SOFR Averages/Index will not be published on Friday, April 3, 2026 due to the March Employment Situation report release and the unavailability of cleared Treasury repo settlement. EFFR and OBFR will publish on April 3 per the Fed's holiday schedule.
key_points: Publication of TGCR, BGCR, SOFR, and SOFR Averages/Index suspended for Friday, April 3, 2026
Suspension caused by unavailability of cleared Treasury repo settlement, eliminating two of three market segments used to calculate Treasury repo reference rates
SIFMA did not recommend full market closure for U.S. government securities trading despite Good Friday
Repo market participants broadly expect to treat April 3 as a holiday
EFFR and OBFR will publish on April 3, 2026 per New York Fed's holiday schedule
On Monday, April 6, 2026, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR will publish reflecting same-day settling Treasury repo transactions that settle Thursday, April 2 and mature Monday, April 6
why_it_matters: This notice informs market participants that key overnight funding rate benchmarks (SOFR, TGCR, BGCR) will have a data gap on April 3 due to the interaction between Good Friday market closures and the March Employment Situation release. Participants using these rates for derivatives pricing, collateral valuations, or loan benchmarking need to adjust their systems and processes accordingly.
market_structure_context: The statement details the mechanics of SOFR calculation and publication schedule. SOFR is derived from three Treasury repo market segments; the unavailability of cleared repo settlement eliminates two segments, making publication unreliable. This highlights the dependency of reference rates on specific market infrastructure and settlement mechanisms.
notes: Source is an official New York Fed operating policy statement with clear, factual information about reference rate publication arrangements. Low risk of inaccuracy. The statement is procedural in nature and does not provide forward-looking commentary on monetary policy or market conditions.
